_comment: Items worn by real characters on poe.ninja, harvested the way src/page-bridge.js does.
kinds.json cannot be relied on to exercise the fallback ladder, and it is not a
matter of picking better items: every item in it came off a trade listing, so at the
moment it was collected the widest query — its own modifiers at 80% of its own rolls
— matched at least the copy it was taken from. One search, one fetch, done. That is
why three separate attempts to speed the ladder up measured as free.
Those items do drift into the ladder as their listings expire, which is worse than
useless: it is the same measurement being made against a different fixture every
week, with nothing in the output to say so until now.
An item somebody is wearing has no such guarantee, and a six-mod rare or a cluster
jewel with three specific notables often has no match at all. That is the point of
these: they miss, the ladder runs, and background-test.mjs prints what it cost.
Measured over these six, 2026-08-05: three missed the wide query, and the ladder
spent 19 of the run's 26 searches. Which three is a property of the market, not of
the file — the run reports it, so read that rather than trusting this line.
To refresh: open a poe.ninja character page with the extension loaded and run
in the page console —
addEventListener('message', (e) => { if (e.data?.source === 'pnc-bridge')
copy(JSON.stringify(e.data.items)); });
postMessage({ source: 'pnc-request' }, '*');
which is the same harvest content.js asks for. Paste items in with a `kind` label
added; background-test.mjs prints which of them reached the ladder, and warns when
none of them do.
Where these came from:
Sergohero-2699/SergoheroGazGaz  (the build where the cluster jewels are slow)
explosivebees-4852/rrrocas      (rare gear, which the top-dps builds do not wear)
